before: Default 'Non-Salary - pacted': a cash car / fuel / maintenance allowance paid under the contract is salary (CST art. 127) unless a written CST art. 128 pact excludes it, and then it is inside the Ley 1393 40% test. after: Default 'Non-Salary - pacted'. before: Statutory-benefit base = No: cash compensation of vacation is not salary (indemnity-like; CST arts. 189, 253, 306; Consejo de Estado, Sala de Consulta, concepto 2027 of 2010). Payroll levies stay Yes (Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17, paid rest). This is an interpretation (no express Supreme Court ruling located); confirm with a labour-law review.
after: Statutory-benefit base and social-security contribution base = No: cash compensation of vacation is not salary but a kind of indemnity (Corte Suprema de Justicia SL467-2019; Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, SU 25185 of 2021, rule 1; CST arts. 189, 253, 306). Payroll levies = Yes: it is paid rest ('descanso remunerado') under Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17 (Consejo de Estado, Sala de Consulta, concepto 2027 of 2010; Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, exp. 27226 of 11 May 2023; UGPP ABC Empleadores 2025 p. 7).

after: Statutory-benefit base and social-security contribution base = No: cash compensation of vacation is not salary but a kind of indemnity (Corte Suprema de Justicia SL467-2019; Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, SU 25185 of 2021, rule 1; CST arts. 189, 253, 306). Payroll levies = Yes: it is paid rest ('descanso remunerado') under Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17 (Consejo de Estado, Sala de Consulta, concepto 2027 of 2010; Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, exp. 27226 of 11 May 2023; UGPP ABC Empleadores 2025 p. 7).

before: Payroll levies = No: Law 21 of 1982 art. 17 limits the levy base to salary elements and paid rest days (Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, SU 25185 of 2021). The incapacity benefit is not salary (CST arts. 128 and 227) and is excluded from the SENA / ICBF / CCF base (Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, 19 August 2021, exp. 23856); an employer-paid top-up of that benefit has the same nature and is not paid rest. UGPP ABC Empleadores 2025 tells employers to take incapacity and maternity values into account for payroll levies; the Consejo de Estado ruling is followed here. Configurable.
after: Payroll levies = No: Law 21 of 1982 art. 17 limits the levy base to salary elements and paid rest days (Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, SU 25185 of 2021). The incapacity benefit is not salary (CST arts. 128 and 227) and is excluded from the SENA / ICBF / CCF base (Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, 19 August 2021, exp. 23856); an employer-paid top-up of that benefit has the same nature and is not paid rest. UGPP ABC Empleadores 2025 (p. 7) tells employers to take incapacity and maternity values into account for payroll levies, while its own table on p. 6 lists these events only for social security; the guide has no normative force and the Consejo de Estado ruling is followed here. Configurable.

Payroll levies = No: the leave is paid by the EPS, not by the employer, so no SENA / ICBF / CCF levies are due on it (Superintendencia del Subsidio Familiar, Concepto 2-2018-083606). The same applies to paternity, shared and flexible parental and childcare leave (rows 331-333; childcare leave is reported in the PILA as an IGE event, Resolucion MSPS 467 de 2025); in flexible parental leave the hours actually worked are ordinary salary. Health and pension contributions continue.

before: (1) The rate for the employer's first two sick days - Decreto 780 de 2016 art. 3.2.1.10 allocates the days but not the rate; Concepto MinSalud 202311602174531 of 20 October 2023 applies CST art. 227 (two thirds); Mercans default 66.67%, configurable. (2) The minimum-wage floor on incapacity payments - Corte Constitucional C-543 de 2007 (the sickness benefit may not fall below the minimum legal wage); Mercans default applies the floor, configurable. after: (1) The rate for the employer's first two sick days - closed: two thirds of salary (CST art. 227, applied to days 1-2 by Concepto MinSalud 202311602174531 of 20 October 2023; Decreto 780 de 2016 art. 3.2.1.10 allocates the days but not the rate); Mercans default 66.67%, configurable for a client that pays 100%. (2) The minimum-wage floor on incapacity payments - closed: Corte Constitucional C-543 de 2007 (the sickness benefit may not fall below the minimum legal wage); the floor is applied, in proportion to the days. (3) The additional employer pension contribution for Decreto Ley 2090 de 2003 high-risk activities - +10 points (art. 5), regime extended by Decreto 1435 de 2025 until Congress legislates; no rule found for workers who started a high-risk activity between 1 January 2025 and that decree.

before: - Severance savings and their interest (casillas 47 to 49) are never withheld, for residents and non-residents alike (Ley 100 de 1993 art. 135 par. 3; DUR 1625 de 2016 art. 1.2.4.1.11), so the six-month average of casilla 59 has no effect on casilla 60. For a non-resident it is reported for completeness; the art. 206 num. 4 exemption is applied, if at all, in the employee's own return (an interpretation).
after: - Severance savings and their interest (casillas 47 to 49) are never withheld, for residents and non-residents alike (Ley 100 de 1993 art. 135 par. 3, extended to every payer by Corte Constitucional C-397 de 1994; DUR 1625 de 2016 art. 1.2.4.1.11), so the six-month average of casilla 59 has no effect on casilla 60. For a non-resident it is reported for completeness; the art. 206 num. 4 exemption is applied, if at all, in the employee's own return (DIAN Concepto 577 de 2020: a non-resident who must file applies ET art. 26 together with arts. 178 and 235-2, which keeps the art. 206 exemptions).

before: Severance savings and their interest are not withheld for a non-resident either (Ley 100 de 1993 art. 135 par. 3; DUR 1625 de 2016 art. 1.2.4.1.11); the art. 206 num. 4 exemption is applied, if at all, in the employee's own return (an interpretation).
after: Severance savings and their interest are not withheld for a non-resident either (Ley 100 de 1993 art. 135 par. 3, extended to every payer by Corte Constitucional C-397 de 1994; DUR 1625 de 2016 art. 1.2.4.1.11); the art. 206 num. 4 exemption is applied, if at all, in the employee's own return (DIAN Concepto 577 de 2020: a non-resident who must file applies ET art. 26 together with arts. 178 and 235-2, which keeps the art. 206 exemptions).

Statutory validation, third pass (text only, no value changes): legal basis of the non-withholding of severance savings and their interest for non-residents (Corte Constitucional C-397 de 1994; DIAN Concepto 577 de 2020) in the Report Matrix and the Example Analysis. Released 2026-11-02 — approved by Wallisson Gomes.
Approved
Wallisson Gomes

The 2026 minimum wage of COP 1,750,905 — a 23% increase over the 2025 figure of COP 1,423,500, a nominal rise of COP 327,405 — was fixed by Decree 1469 of 29 December 2025. That decree was provisionally suspended by the Council of State (Section Two, Subsection A) in annulment proceeding 11001-03-25-000-2026-00004-00 by order of 12 February 2026, and the Government complied by issuing Decree 0159 of 19 February 2026, which re-fixed the identical amount transitorily. Decree 1469 of 2025 therefore recovered full force and is the operative instrument as at the date of this guide, with Decree 0159 of 2026 spent.

before: The minimum-wage floor on incapacity payments. Where 66.67% of the employee's salary falls below the minimum wage, market practice and settled administrative doctrine top the payment up to one minimum wage. Mercans default: apply the floor, configurable. Corte Constitucional Sentencia C-543 de 2007 holds that the monetary sickness benefit (auxilio monetario por enfermedad de origen común) may never fall below the minimum legal wage (resolutive part: the benefit "no podrá ser inferior al salario mínimo legal vigente").
after: The minimum-wage floor on incapacity payments. Where 66.67% of the employee's salary falls below the minimum wage, the payment is topped up to one minimum wage, in proportion to the days of incapacity. Corte Constitucional Sentencia C-543 de 2007 holds that the monetary sickness benefit (auxilio monetario por enfermedad de origen común) may never fall below the minimum legal wage (resolutive part: the benefit "no podrá ser inferior al salario mínimo legal vigente").
